sentences.text: It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners had earlier bought certain land from the erstwhile tenure holders namely Ramdas, Suraj Lal and Sangam Lal through registered sale deed on 22.6.2018 and on the basis thereof the names were entered in the revenue record.
The sale deed mentions the boundaries of such land.
The sellers/previous owners also sold certain land to the opposite party no. 4 and his brother.

The opposite party no. 4 has lodged the impugned FIR alleging that the petitioners are Bhu-Mafia, who having bought a land situated adjacent to the land of opposite party no. 4, wanted them to give 'Rasta' from the land of the informant and tried to take forceful possession thereof, when the informant refused the petitioners,
it is alleged, in collusion with the erstwhile tenure holders, the petitioners again obtained the sale deed of land of the informant/opposite party no. 4 on 10.6.2022 by playing fraud and mentioning the boundaries of land which belong to the informant and of which he was in possession.

During the course of argument, it has been stated by the learned counsel for the petitioners that Gata No. 149 is a large plot of land and has been subdivided by the erstwhile tenure holders and sold off to several parts including the petitioners and informant.
Since it is a large plot of land, the boundaries, having not been clearly demarcated, are shown as the same in all sale deeds including that of the petitioners and of the informant.

Sri Dinesh Kumar, who appears for the opposite party no. 4, has pointed that when the petitioners tried to interfere in the possession of land belonging to the informant, they have also filed an injunction suit wherein an interim injunction has also been granted in their favour.

It has been stated that the petitioners only to harass the informant and to take over possession of land belonging to the informant have fraudulently mentioned the same boundaries in their sale deed be executed in June, 2022 as are the boundaries mentioned in the sale deed of the informant.

It has further been submitted by the learned counsel for the opposite party no. 4 that the Gata No.
149 has not been formally partitioned/divided into plots of land as alleged to have been sold by the erstwhile tenure holders and each person who is a co-tenure holder is deemed to be the owner of the entire gata till such formal partition/demarcation is carried out.
No application for demarcation has been moved by the petitioners of their land initially bought by them allegedly in 2018 from the recorded tenure holders.

This Court having heard the learned counsel for both the parties, is of the opinion that both the parties should file application for demarcation before the Revenue Authorities to get their land measured and demarcated.

sentences.text: The opposite party no. 4 cannot be forced to file a suit for declaration of subsequent sale deeds as void and pursue unending litigation in the Civil Court due to the fraudulent action of the petitioners.

After having examined the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and perused the impugned FIR, we are of the opinion that the impugned FIR discloses cognizable offence against the petitioners, hence, no interference is called for by this Court in its extraordinary power under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for quashing of the FIR or for grant of any interim relief to the petitioners and accordingly, the present writ petition is dismissed.
